stimulus.body: In 2005 a study of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% of scores varied with family background, while 30% varied with school resources alone.

questions.stem: Explain the 2005 Africa finding about educational inequality.

answer.exemplar: In 2005 a study of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% of scores varied with family background, while 30% varied with school resources alone. This illustrates educational inequality: unequal educational outcomes linked to social background. A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person, and it distinguishes this idea from competing accounts that locate the cause elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates educational inequality: unequal educational outcomes linked to social background. The 58 percent versus 30 percent split in West Africa shows why this reading fits better than the alternatives.
questions.hint: Think about the social force behind the two figures.

stimulus.body: In 2007 a study of 450 retirees in West Africa found 65% of scores varied with family background, while 33% varied with school resources alone.

questions.stem: What is the point gap in the 2007 Africa educational inequality survey?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 33 percent from 65 percent gives 32 percentage points, the gap reported in the 2007 data from West Africa between the two shares.
questions.hint: Look past the numbers to the relationship they describe.
